ireland/trinity-book-of-kells.name: Trinity College and the Book of Kells
ireland/trinity-book-of-kells.description: The ninth-century illuminated gospel and the Long Room library.
ireland/trinity-book-of-kells.details: Trinity College Dublin holds the Book of Kells and the Long Room, a barrel-vaulted library with 200,000 old books. Tickets are timed and sell out in summer. The campus is in the middle of the city and a good start for a walking tour.

ireland/guinness-pubs.name: Guinness Storehouse and Dublin pubs
ireland/guinness-pubs.description: The brewery experience with a pint on the rooftop, plus traditional music pubs in Temple Bar.
ireland/guinness-pubs.details: The Guinness Storehouse tells the story of the famous stout and ends at the Gravity Bar with a view of Dublin. Temple Bar is touristy, so try quieter pubs such as The Cobblestone for live traditional music. Book the Storehouse online.

ireland/kilmainham-gaol.name: Kilmainham Gaol and Phoenix Park
ireland/kilmainham-gaol.description: The prison where leaders of the 1916 Rising were held, with a guided tour.
ireland/kilmainham-gaol.details: Kilmainham Gaol is a major site in Irish history, visited on a guided tour only, and tickets must be booked in advance. Phoenix Park nearby is one of the largest city parks in Europe and has wild deer. Allow half a day.

ireland/wicklow-glendalough.name: Glendalough and Wicklow Mountains
ireland/wicklow-glendalough.description: A monastic valley with a round tower and two lakes, an hour south of Dublin.
ireland/wicklow-glendalough.details: Glendalough was founded by St Kevin in the 6th century and has a round tower, a ruined cathedral and lakeside walks. The Wicklow Mountains are the Garden of Ireland. Trails range from easy to long hikes. Tour buses run from Dublin.

ireland/newgrange.name: Newgrange passage tomb
ireland/newgrange.description: A 5,000-year-old burial mound older than Stonehenge, with a winter solstice alignment.
ireland/newgrange.details: Newgrange in the Boyne Valley is a Neolithic passage tomb with a white quartz facade. Visitors enter the chamber on a guided tour from the visitor centre, so booking ahead is essential. It is about an hour north of Dublin.

ireland/cliffs-of-moher-burren.name: Cliffs of Moher and the Burren
ireland/cliffs-of-moher-burren.description: Sea cliffs rising 214 metres above the Atlantic, plus a limestone moonscape nearby.
ireland/cliffs-of-moher-burren.details: The Cliffs of Moher have a visitor centre and cliff-top paths, and the O Brien tower. Check local access notices, because sections are sometimes closed for safety. The Burren is a limestone plateau with rare wildflowers and ancient tombs. Wind is strong, so dress warmly.

ireland/aran-islands.name: Aran Islands
ireland/aran-islands.description: Remote Atlantic islands of stone walls, Irish speakers and an ancient fort.
ireland/aran-islands.details: Inis Mor, the largest Aran island, can be explored by bike or minibus. Dun Aonghasa is a prehistoric cliff fort. A ferry from Rossaveal or Doolin takes about 40 minutes. Weather can cancel sailings. Wear windproof clothing.

ireland/galway-connemara.name: Galway city and Connemara
ireland/galway-connemara.description: A lively west-coast city of buskers and pubs, with a wild mountain and lake landscape nearby.
ireland/galway-connemara.details: Galway has colourful streets, the Spanish Arch and traditional music pubs. Connemara is a day trip of bog, mountains and lakes, with Kylemore Abbey as the star. The Wild Atlantic Way coast road is scenic. Pubs fill quickly on weekends.

ireland/ring-of-kerry.name: Ring of Kerry
ireland/ring-of-kerry.description: A 179-kilometre scenic loop of coast, mountains and lakes on the Iveragh Peninsula.
ireland/ring-of-kerry.details: The Ring of Kerry is usually driven anticlockwise to avoid tour buses. Stops include Killarney National Park, Ladies View, Sneem and Waterville, with the Skellig Michael boats from Portmagee (seasonal). A full day is best.

ireland/dingle-peninsula.name: Dingle Peninsula and Slea Head Drive
ireland/dingle-peninsula.description: A narrow western peninsula of beehive huts, beaches and the town of Dingle.
ireland/dingle-peninsula.details: Slea Head Drive has views of the Blasket Islands, ancient stone huts and Gaelic-speaking villages. Dingle town has fishing boats, pubs with live music and Fungie memorials. The roads are narrow, so drive slowly.

ireland/killarney-national-park.name: Killarney National Park and Gap of Dunloe
ireland/killarney-national-park.description: Lakes, woodland and a famous mountain pass, explored by jaunting car or hike.
ireland/killarney-national-park.details: Killarney National Park has Muckross House and gardens, Torc Waterfall and Ross Castle. The Gap of Dunloe is a glacial pass reached by walking or pony and trap. Weather is changeable, so take waterproofs.

ireland/cork-blarney.name: Cork city, English Market and Blarney Castle
ireland/cork-blarney.description: Ireland second city with a covered food market, and a castle where you kiss the stone.
ireland/cork-blarney.details: Cork City has the English Market, a 1788 covered market with local produce. Blarney Castle is 20 minutes away, with gardens and the Blarney Stone. The Rock of Cashel in Tipperary lies on the way from Dublin.
